elements.title: Marie Denizard (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Marie Denizard (pictured) stood as a candidate in a French presidential election in 1913, thirty years before French women achieved suffrage?

elements.title: The Crystal (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that The Crystal was one of few publications in early-20th-century China that regularly covered same-sex intimacy?

elements.title: Hanif Kureshi (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Hanif Kureshi transformed shadows cast by the Sun into street art?

elements.title: Gigarta (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Gigarta, a settlement mentioned by Strabo and Pliny the Elder, is believed to have been located on the slopes of Mount Lebanon, although its exact location remains under debate?

elements.title: Al LeBoeuf (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Al LeBoeuf was diagnosed with a rare condition in 2012 from an injury that he suffered in 1985?

elements.title: Eurovision Song Contest 1975 (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the Swedish broadcaster organising the Eurovision Song Contest 1975 refused to allow the contest to be shown in Chile, as a protest against the country's military dictatorship?

elements.title: Polish manga and anime fandom (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the Polish manga and anime fandom arose in the 1990s and now numbers over 100,000 people?

elements.title: Frank A. Kimball (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Frank A. Kimball brought a transcontinental rail terminus to National City, California, in exchange for thousands of acres of land?

elements.title: feelies (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Aldous Huxley developed his "feelies" in response to the emergence of "talkies"?
